subject: CareWorks: SDK & Auth checklist + model routing fallback proposal
messages:
From: Sara Holden <sara.holden@careworks.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@careworks.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: SDK/auth questions from today

Thanks for the demo this morning — good discussion. Two technical follow-ups from our infra team so we can scope the PoC: 

1) SDKs: we primarily run Node (server) and a small Python analytics pipeline. Do you have a recommended SDK initialization pattern for server-side usage (connection pooling, retries) and for short-lived worker processes? Any sample config for region pinning?

2) Auth: we need options that integrate with our existing Okta OIDC identity provider and also a service-account pattern for backend-to-backend calls. What's supported today and recommended for a 1-month PoC?

3) Routing & fallbacks: our latency SLO for the UI is 250ms p50 and 600ms p95 for single-turn prompts. We want to automatically fall back to a cheaper model variant during congestion, but only if quality doesn't regress beyond an agreed threshold. Can you share how Redwood implements latency/cost policies and how we can test them?

4) Embeddings & rerankers: we plan to index internal docs and use a reranker for top-k. Any guidance on embedding model selection and recommended batch sizes?

We're attaching a draft internal checklist and would like a concise proposed architecture we can share with infra by EOD tomorrow.

--
Sara Holden
Head of Platform
CareWorks Health
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: SDK/auth questions from today

Sara — thanks for the clear list. High level answers + a proposed minimal PoC architecture below. Attaching a lightweight checklist (careworks_sdk_auth_checklist.xlsx) and a draft fallback policy (careworks_fallback_policy_v1.md).

Quick answers:
- SDKs: Redwood Node + Python SDKs support long-lived client instances. For server-side we recommend a pool of 2-4 clients per worker node with request-level timeouts and circuit-breaker (sample config attached). For short-lived workers use ephemeral clients with warmup (init + first-call latency accounted in your SLO). We’ll share a code snippet in the PoC repo.

- Auth: supported: API keys (for quick PoC), mTLS (dedicated), and OIDC via Okta for user-context tokens. For backend-to-backend we recommend OIDC service accounts (client_credentials) exchanged to short-lived Redwood tokens; easiest for PoC: API keys scoped to environment with rotation. We can enable Okta OIDC integration in the Private/Dedicated flows if you need user-level auditing.

- Routing & fallbacks: Redwood supports policy-driven routing by latency and cost. You can declare a primary route (gpt-like high-quality model in us-east) and fallback chains to a quantized low-cost variant. Policies are rule-based: e.g., if p95_latency > 550ms or queue depth > 50, route to fallback. Quality guards are attached to rollouts: we evaluate on a small labeled prompt set and block fallback if quality drop > 3 BLEU/ROUGE-ish equivalent for your metric. For PoC we recommend a canary that ramps 10->50->100% with monitored evals.

- Embeddings & rerankers: recommend medium-size embedding for search recall (cost/latency tradeoff). Batch sizes: start with 64–128 for offline indexing; 8–32 for real-time user queries depending on your latency target. Reranker runs on top-k (k=50) with a small cross-encoder. We can provide pre-benchmarked pairings.

Proposed minimal PoC (deliverables in 2 weeks):
- Redwood-hosted route in us-east primary, eu-west as DR.
- SDK quickstart repo: node + python examples (pooling + retries).
- Auth: API-key PoC + Okta OIDC integration doc for next phase.
- Routing policy draft: primary -> quantized-fallback chain, latency thresholds, canary schedule.
- Eval harness: 200 labeled prompts for quality gate.

Next steps: 1) Dev sync Tues 6/22 10–11am PT to walk checklist + sample config; 2) PoC kickoff once infra approves API-key pattern. Please confirm if Tues works and whether we should loop in your security lead.

Adding implementation-level notes for the PoC that I’ll bring to the dev sync: 

1) Sample SDK config (Node):
- client = new RedwoodClient({
    region: 'us-east-1',
    maxSockets: 50,
    requestTimeoutMs: 1200,
    retryPolicy: { attempts: 3, backoffMs: 200 }
  })
- Use an internal connection pool per process. Warmup call on deploy to populate KV caches.

2) Auth flow options:
- Quick PoC: environment-scoped API key -> header x-rdwd-key.
- Next step: Okta client_credentials -> exchange for short-lived Redwood token (15m). We'll provide a sample token-exchange lambda.

3) Routing & fallback config (policy DSL excerpt):
- primary: model=redwood-aquila-1, region=us-east-1
- fallback_chain: [redwood-aquila-1-quant, redwood-sparrow-lite]
- triggers: if p95_latency > 550ms OR queue_length > 40 OR error_rate > 2%
- quality_gate: run on eval set every 30m; allow fallback if measured CTR_delta < 2% (your metric)

4) Embeddings pipeline:
- Bulk indexing: batch=128, threads=8; store vectors in your managed vector DB (we recommend Pinecone/FAISS on your infra).
- Real-time queries: batch=16 for embedding generation, rerank top-50 using cross-encoder (quantized where possible).

5) Observability: We'll provision a per-route dashboard showing token cost, latency histograms, and top-10 prompts causing fallbacks. You'll get alerts for quality regressions and fallback spikes.

Attaching the two files to the thread; I can put the DSL snippet into the PoC repo before the sync.

--
Dev Patel

Redwood Inference

Thanks — everything looks reasonable. Two quick asks before our Tues sync: 

1) Security: can you send a short doc that maps the API-key PoC to our SOC 2 controls (rotation, access logging, revocation)? Our security lead wants that before approving any keys in staging.

2) Canary window: we prefer a 1-week canary in staging with 0->10% traffic ramp and a kill-switch to revert instantly to primary. Can Redwood automate a timeboxed canary (start/stop) and provide a single-button rollback in the console?

If you can drop the SOC2 mapping and confirm the canary automation by EOD Monday we can confirm the sync and loop in our security lead.

--
Luis Ortega

CareWorks Health
